governance.constitution:
- Organize Refine as Foundation, Capabilities, and Surfaces. Foundation holds the durable concepts, Capabilities own the powers and product semantics, and Surfaces remain replaceable adapters.
- Keep the foundation small and legible: Nodes, Goals, Features, target-app context, workflow state, settings, and evidence must remain explicit enough for people and agents to inspect.
- Keep Process, Agents, and Workflow as shared capabilities. They may evolve or be replaced, but their responsibilities and composition must remain coherent across the system.
- Preserve local ownership. Authoritative state, Git history, settings, runtime records, and agent output must be inspectable and recoverable; caches and projections must remain derived.
- Be agent-first by using installed coding-agent CLIs and host tools through shared configuration, process supervision, workflow, and evidence rather than provider- or surface-specific product paths.
- Treat workflow as durable state advancement, process as the observable execution substrate, and agents as actors that use both without redefining either.
- Prefer mitigation and accountability over broad capability denial: isolation, Git, governance, quality, review, visible errors, and recovery should make powerful work safe enough to use.
- Preserve room for architectural discovery. A better design may replace current machinery when it explains the tradeoff, protects product intent, and supplies proportionate migration and verification evidence.
governance.product: Refine is a local-first, agent-first operating layer for software delivery. It turns understandable Goals and Features into reviewable changes by coordinating explicit workflow state, supervised processes, installed coding-agent CLIs, Git isolation, quality, governance, and durable evidence across one or many Nodes. Its core promise is that powerful autonomous work remains user-owned, inspectable, recoverable, and consistent across replaceable human and agent surfaces.

rules.text: Respect the Foundation-Capabilities-Surfaces boundary: durable concepts belong in the model and target-app foundation, product behavior and orchestration belong in shared capabilities, and UI, CLI, API, desktop, and agent surfaces stay thin and semantically consistent.

Compose the existing Process, Agents, Workflow, Git, state, quality, governance, and evidence capabilities before creating new machinery. Each concern should have one authoritative implementation and source of truth unless the Goal explicitly proposes an architectural replacement.

Keep authoritative target-app state local, durable, inspectable, and outside the primary source worktree; keep runtime artifacts separate and projections or caches rebuildable. State-layout changes require a compatible migration or explicit transition plan.

Run agents, Git, quality, lifecycle, and long work through the supervised process substrate, with explicit ownership, status, logs, cancellation, failures, and recovery. When activating a new Refine build requires replacing or restarting that supervisor, a restart-safe handoff may run outside it and independently complete the upgrade. The handoff must retain durable, operation-correlated ownership and state, visible progress and failures, and restart, rollback, and recovery reconciliation.

Coordinate parallel or distributed work explicitly through Node ownership, workflow claims and capacity, dependency or Feature ordering, and isolated Git branches or worktrees so concurrent changes remain reviewable and recoverable.

Require evidence proportional to actual architectural and operational risk. Verify the affected behavior with the smallest focused checks that provide confidence, including integration or failure-path evidence when a change alters concurrency, persistence, process, Git, release, recovery, or cross-surface semantics. Update only affected docs/intent pages when documented product intent or an architectural contract changes; do not require unrelated documentation or broad cleanup.

Allow architectural evolution when a Goal states the protected product intent, explains why the new design is better, updates capability boundaries and intent docs, and provides migration, compatibility, and verification evidence proportionate to the change.

Keep Refine agent-first: delegate adaptable reasoning and execution to installed agents through shared context and tools instead of duplicating it in bespoke product logic or surface-specific controls. Add first-class functionality when it provides durable coordination, state, synchronization, supervision, evidence, recovery, accessibility, deterministic integrity, or a materially better shared human and agent surface; preserve one capability across UI, CLI, API, and MCP.

Use SSE as the only mechanism for live browser updates. UI code must not use periodic polling, retry loops, timers, or repeated status GETs to observe background work or state changes; use one-shot authoritative reads only for initial load, operation registration race closure, reconnect reconciliation, or explicit user refresh.

governance.constitution:
- Refine's components are model (entities), process (supervisor to manage running processes), prompts (LLM templates), surfaces (interfaces into refine), tools (reusable functions for workflow steps), and workflow (defined workflow which calls out to tools). These map directly to src/[model| process|prompts|surfaces|tools|workflow].
- Refine uses a flat file persistence, file-based indexes, in-memory caching, and Rust to maintain high performance. Ensure <50ms performance on CLI and API calls (assuming we are not waiting on LLMs or outside tools).
- Ensure that the architecture is maintained and is consistent. Do not invent new architectural concepts; instead, follow the existing architecture.
- Ensure that documentation, especially src/intent/*, is maintained and the existing document format is preserved.
- Ensure Refine remains "agent-first" by using installed coding-agent CLIs. Do not duplicate coding agent functionality.
governance.product: Refine is a local-first, agent-first operating layer for software delivery. It moves user-defined Goals through a workflow to ensure parallel implementation across Nodes, quality, and governance.

rules.text: Keep component code within `src/{model,process,prompts,surfaces,tools,workflow}` and extend existing architecture instead of inventing new concepts.
Preserve Rust-based flat-file persistence, file indexes, and in-memory caching; keep non-external CLI/API work under 50ms.
Update affected documentation—especially `src/intent/*`—without changing its established format.
Use installed coding-agent CLIs for coding-agent capabilities; do not reimplement them.

findings.description: The retained tests do not establish the lifecycle outcome claimed by P1. paused_workflow_suppresses_background_repository_workers_until_resumed only calls set_workflow_paused(false) and asserts the flag is false; it never launches a worker after resume. running_background_repository_workers_quiesce_at_pause_boundaries uses an empty runtime/registry, so it proves loop exit but not that a paused worker avoids a real scan/sync/cleanup side effect or that work resumes afterward.
findings.recommendation: Retain those tests, then add deterministic instrumentation or fixtures that observe a repository-operation boundary: prove no scan/sync/cleanup occurs after pause, prove both workers settle successfully, clear the gate, run supervision/dispatch again, and prove each worker becomes live or performs its next eligible operation. Keep shared-host tests serial.

findings.description: The candidate's HTTP supervision uses a separate background_automation_paused check before ensure_background_worker. Pause can be set between those calls, causing ensure_background_worker to return the expected paused Conflict and the cleanup supervisor to report it as a failure. The Git-sync loop also treats every pause-state read error like a pause through matches!(..., Ok(false)), silently suppressing Git sync on corrupt or unreadable control state. P1 currently proposes replaying this behavior unchanged.
findings.recommendation: Make supervision consume a single explicit ensure outcome, or classify a paused Conflict as expected after re-reading the canonical gate. Distinguish Ok(true), Ok(false), and Err for Git sync and report genuine pause-state errors consistently. Add focused tests around pause-at-launch and unreadable/invalid pause state so expected pause is quiet but faults remain observable.

findings.description: P2 promises consistent observed process state but does not include src/tools/observability/processes.rs. Today runner_work_summary overwrites every synthetic runner row with paused whenever workflow_paused is true, including an already-running merger or plan extraction operation, while background_processes_stopped and agents_paused are emitted as true compatibility aliases even though active Goal agents continue and only selected repository workers quiesce. The existing route test reinforces this by asserting every runner_work row is paused.
findings.recommendation: Explicitly scope the projection work. Preserve legacy aliases only as documented compatibility fields, keep workflow_paused as canonical, and avoid replacing the observed status of an already-active operation with cosmetic paused state. Add projection tests for a live Agent/operation during pause, quiesced Git-sync and cleanup workers, and accurate state after resume.

findings.description: The proposed focused verification does not test what it claims. cargo test --lib web_server_serves_project_utility_upgrade_health_and_sse_routes selects the unrelated utility-route test at project.rs:4; the pause/active-Goal assertions are in web_server_lists_processes_and_updates_pause_controls at project.rs:368. Likewise the catalog test module has no workflow pause/resume description assertion, so cargo test --lib surfaces::cli::catalog::tests:: can pass while the CLI wording is wrong. Static source matching alone would also not execute the pause/unpause direction and payload decision.
findings.recommendation: Run the actual pause route test by its exact name, add a catalog assertion for the workflow pause and resume about strings (or inspect refine commands JSON explicitly), and extract a pure web pause-action model returning direction, confirmation copy, and {paused: boolean} payload so Node tests execute both pause and unpause paths before separately asserting delegation to /api/workflow/pause.

findings.description: P4 says it will preserve the retained Round 1 branch/worktree/reflog, but the Round 1 worktree path and its Git worktree metadata are already absent. The commit, branch ref, and reflog do exist. Its listed final git status and diff stat checks also do not prove that the retained branch ref stayed at the original SHA.
findings.recommendation: Record an initial evidence inventory instead of promising preservation of a nonexistent worktree. Capture the exact Round 1 ref SHA and reflog head before replay, repeat the reads after implementation, assert both still identify f306cbf9e8b520146e4f75a73e2e3592f9d4bc8f, and report the pre-existing worktree absence without attempting to recreate, delete, or rewrite retained evidence.

result.summary: Revise the proposed plan before implementation. Preserve the clean replay strategy and cross-surface wording work, but add real worker resume evidence, make pause-aware supervision race-safe and observable, explicitly reconcile process projection truth, correct the focused verification commands, exercise pause action behavior through testable helpers, and inventory retained evidence accurately.

affected_behavior: Git-sync launch, dispatch, repository-operation boundary, cooperative quiescence, and post-resume work
Automatic inactive-worktree-cleanup launch, dispatch, scan/cleanup boundary, cooperative quiescence, and post-resume work
Race-safe HTTP daemon supervision and observable pause-control read failures
checklist.description: Replay the six clean-applying Rust implementation patches from retained commit f306cbf9e8b520146e4f75a73e2e3592f9d4bc8f without cherry-picking, amending, or moving that commit, then harden the recovered runner lifecycle. Keep workflow_paused as the sole gate for Git-sync and automatic inactive-worktree-cleanup launch, direct dispatch, and active-loop safe boundaries. Replace paused-as-Conflict and caller-side prechecks with an explicit ensure result such as Running versus Paused, so a pause between supervision checks is an expected quiet outcome and a child launched during the race immediately exits successfully at dispatch. Make every pause read distinguish unpaused, paused, and error; propagate or report corrupt/unreadable control state rather than treating it as pause. Adapt HTTP Git-sync and cleanup supervision to consume the single ensure result and report only real faults. Retain the candidate tests and add deterministic test seams at the actual scan/sync/cleanup boundary: block each worker before its consequential operation, set pause, release it, prove no operation occurred and both loops settled successfully, clear pause, supervise or dispatch again, and prove each worker reaches or performs its next eligible repository operation.
checklist.governance_rationale: Guidance 0 applies because the shared Process capability must own admission and quiescence while daemon/API availability and active Goal execution remain separate. Guidance 1 applies by extending the existing runner, dispatch, and supervision responsibilities with small cohesive outcome/boundary helpers instead of adding a parallel pause subsystem; the large Processes JavaScript file will be reviewed for cohesion and only split if the new pure action model creates a genuinely separate responsibility.
verification: Observed before implementation: git diff f306cbf9e8b520146e4f75a73e2e3592f9d4bc8f^ f306cbf9e8b520146e4f75a73e2e3592f9d4bc8f -- src/process/runner.rs src/process/runner/dispatch.rs src/process/runner/git_sync.rs src/process/runner/worktree_cleanup.rs src/process/runner/tests.rs src/surfaces/web_server/http/background_loops.rs | git apply --check --verbose -> all six patches reported Checking patch with no error.

cargo test --lib process::runner::tests:: -- --test-threads=1 -> report exact passed/failed/ignored counts, including retained launch/quiescence tests plus deterministic no-side-effect, successful-settlement, post-resume-operation, pause-at-ensure, and invalid-pause-state cases.

cargo test --lib pause -- --test-threads=1 -> report exact serial pause-related counts and prove paused is an expected ensure outcome while corrupt or unreadable process-control state remains an error.
Focused supervision classification tests -> paused outcomes produce no failure text; pause-state parsing/IO errors produce an observable supervision error for both Git-sync and worktree cleanup.
